Apis mellifera

The western honey bee: one queen, tens of thousands of sisters, and a hive that thinks as one.

Honey bees have lived alongside people for thousands of years. This guide covers how a colony is organised, how foragers share directions, how honey is made, and what threatens the bees today.

Topics

  • The colony and its castes

    One queen, thousands of workers and a few hundred drones make up a single superorganism.

  • The waggle dance

    Foragers tell nestmates where to find flowers using a figure-eight dance on the comb.

  • Honey and wax comb

    Nectar becomes honey through enzymes and evaporation, then is stored in hexagonal wax cells.

  • Threats and how to help

    Varroa mites, pesticides, disease and habitat loss all put pressure on honey bees.
